summary: Pinned session reverts during tiered canary: sidecar snapshot desync triggers fallback routing
description: Issue summary: During a staged (tiered) canary rollout for redwood-open-gpt-3.5-v1, a subset of tenant sessions that were previously pinned to the promoted variant unexpectedly reverted to the default fallback variant. Impact: customer-visible mixed-model responses for ~3% of requests from Meridian Analytics' production traffic in us-east; increased latency for affected requests due to additional routing and KV cache misses. Timeline: 2026-03-10 09:10 UTC - deploy start for tiered canary; 09:22 UTC - first customer report; 09:30-10:00 UTC - increased 5xxs and quality complaints; 10:15 UTC - Support triage. Observed behavior: some sessions lost model affinity and were routed to a fallback variant; this coincided with sidecar snapshot refresh events on a subset of edge pods. Expected behavior: pin affinity should persist across sidecar snapshot refreshes and control-plane rollouts until explicit unpin or pin TTL expiry. Steps to reproduce: 1) Create tiered canary rollout with staged weights and pin variant for a test tenant; 2) Trigger sidecar config refresh (simulated by restarting sidecar or pushing a SIGHUP); 3) Send session traffic with pinned token and observe routing; 4) Reproduce by toggling edge header rewrite feature flag. Logs & artifacts: edge-proxy logs show header rewrite events at same timestamps as routing flips; sidecar snapshot logs show a full snapshot replace (snapshot_id changed) and an applied config hash mismatch with control-plane; KV cache miss logs for pinned sessions; sample request IDs: rq-0a1f23, rq-0a1f98, rq-0b2c11. Attachments: packet captures and a short trace are in the ticket attachments (internal).
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: sidecar snapshot replace caused pin metadata to be dropped locally on edge pods that applied new snapshot before pin reconciliation completed.
Correlated timing between snapshot replace and a partial control-plane propagation delay (10-14s window) in us-east region.
Found header rewrite rule that migrates legacy session-cookie to new token format; during rewrite the pin-token field was being stripped by an older sidecar build on ~7% of pods.
Reproduced in the staging cluster by applying an older sidecar image plus the header rewrite: pinned token removed on snapshot apply and route fallback triggered.
Checked rollout orchestration logs: canary weight adjust and snapshot distribution overlapped; reconciliation controller did not retry pin sync fast enough when snapshot applied mid-window.
No evidence of model-serving node eviction or GPU preemption; serving runtime healthy for promoted variant.

root_cause: A race between sidecar snapshot replacement and control-plane pin-reconciliation caused pin metadata to be stripped on edge pods running an older sidecar build that applied an incompatible header rewrite. The strip led to routing logic treating the session as unpinned, invoking fallback routing to a default variant.
workaround: Disabled the header rewrite flag for affected tenant during the canary window and ran a targeted pin-resync job against edge pods in us-east. This restored session affinity for affected tenants within ~30 minutes.
resolution_plan: Short term: keep header rewrite disabled for Meridian until sidecar patch is deployed. Medium term: merge sidecar PR to preserve pin-token across rewrite and add a forced pin-sync when snapshot ID changes; add critical telemetry and an alert on pin-drop rates. Long term: adjust rollout orchestration to avoid snapshot distributions that can overlap with active pin windows or make reconciliation immediate on snapshot increment.
notes: Customer is on a Dedicated contract; follow-up retrospective scheduled with product and infra teams to update the canary runbook and add explicit guidance about header rewrites during pin-sensitive rollouts.
